problem_statement: The devicetree API must provide macros that query whether register names exist across instances of a compatible. Specifically, a macro that reports whether any status-okay instance of a given compatible has a register with a given name, and a macro that reports whether all status-okay instances have such a register (returning true when no instances exist). These must behave correctly for names present in some instances but not all, names only in disabled instances, and names that do not exist at all, and must be usable in compile-time conditionals.

Adding the two names (and noting they take a single register-name argument) is sufficient and does not reveal the implementation.

problem_statement_fixed: The devicetree API must provide two macros that query whether register names exist across instances of a compatible. Specifically, a macro named DT_ANY_INST_REG_HAS_NAME_STATUS_OKAY that reports whether any status-okay instance of a given compatible has a register with a given name, and a macro named DT_ALL_INST_REG_HAS_NAME_STATUS_OKAY that reports whether all status-okay instances have such a register (returning 1 when no instances exist). These must behave correctly for names present in some instances but not all, names only in disabled instances, and names that do not exist at all, and must be usable in compile-time conditionals (e.g. COND_CODE_1, COND_CODE_0, IS_ENABLED, IF_ENABLED). Each macro takes a single argument: the register name as a lowercase-and-underscores token (e.g. foo, bar, baz).
